question:
Which of the following statement is correct?

I. The biggest state of India in terms of area is Uttar Pradesh.

II. Rajasthan is the state of India which have highest population among all other states of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are factually incorrect, so neither statement is correct. (सबसे बड़ा राज्य — राजस्थान)

 

• Statement I is wrong: The largest state of India by area is Rajasthan (about 3.42 lakh sq. km), not Uttar Pradesh. Uttar Pradesh is actually the largest state by population.

 

• Statement II is wrong: The state with the highest population is Uttar Pradesh, not Rajasthan. As per Census 2011, UP's population is around 19.98 crore, far ahead of any other state.

 

• Rajasthan ranks 7th in population, while Madhya Pradesh (not Rajasthan or UP) is the second largest state by area after Rajasthan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Order of Indian states by area (largest to smallest, top 3): Rajasthan > Madhya Pradesh > Maharashtra.

 

• Order of Indian states by population (Census 2011, top 3): Uttar Pradesh > Maharashtra > Bihar.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect because Statement I itself is factually wrong (UP is not the largest state by area).

 

• Only II (Option 3): Incorrect because Statement II itself is factually wrong (Rajasthan does not have the highest population).

 

• Both I and II (Option 4): Incorrect because both statements, not just one, are factually wrong.

question: Who among the following is Telangana's first Sangeet Natak Akademi Award winner?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padmaja Reddy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Padmaja Reddy is a renowned Kuchipudi dancer and is recognised as Telangana's first Sangeet Natak Akademi Award winner. (संगीत नाटक अकादमी पुरस्कार — पद्मजा रेड्डी)

 

• She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for her contribution to Kuchipudi dance, and also runs the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Hyderabad.

 

• She was also honoured with the Padma Shri in 2023 for her contribution to art.

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's national academy for music, dance and drama, and its annual awards (Akademi Puraskar) are the highest Indian recognition given to practising artists.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi was set up in 1952 and is India's first national akademi for the arts, functioning under the Ministry of Culture.

 

• Other prominent Kuchipudi exponents include Yamini Reddy (Padmaja Reddy's daughter) and the legendary Vempati Chinna Satyam.

 

NOTE

 

• Yamini Reddy (Option 2): A leading Kuchipudi dancer and daughter of Padmaja Reddy, but she is not Telangana's first Sangeet Natak Akademi awardee.

 

• Deepa Sashindran (Option 3): A Bharatanatyam dancer, not associated with this distinction.

 

• Shantala Shivalingappa (Option 4): An acclaimed Kuchipudi dancer of Indian-French origin, not connected to Telangana's first award.

question: Who among the following became the first Asian to win the award for best sound for the documentary 'India's Daughter' at the coveted Motion Picture Sound Editors' 63rd annual Golden Reel Awards?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Resul Pookutty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Resul Pookutty, the Oscar-winning Indian sound designer, became the first Asian to win the Golden Reel Award for Best Sound Editing for the BBC documentary 'India's Daughter' at the 63rd Motion Picture Sound Editors' (MPSE) Golden Reel Awards in 2016. (गोल्डन रील पुरस्कार — रसूल पूकुट्टी)

 

• The award was given in the Feature Documentary category, and Pookutty's win made him the first Asian sound professional to receive this honour.

 

• Pookutty is widely known in India for winning the Academy Award (Oscar) for Best Sound Mixing for 'Slumdog Millionaire' (2009), along with Ian Tapp and Richard Pryke.

 

• 'India's Daughter', directed by Leslee Udwin, is a documentary based on the 2012 Nirbhaya (Delhi gang rape) case.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Resul Pookutty has also worked on films like Black, Jodhaa Akbar, and Raavan, and has received the National Film Award for Best Audiography multiple times.

 

• The Motion Picture Sound Editors (MPSE) is a US-based honorary society that recognises excellence in sound editing across film, television and documentaries.

 

NOTE

 

• Justin Jose (Option 1): Not associated with this Golden Reel Award win.

 

• P.M.Satheesh (Option 3): Not the recipient of this particular award.

 

• Boby John (Option 4): Not associated with this achievement.

question: Which of the following is known as 'Plaster of Paris'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2CaSO4.H2O.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Plaster of Paris (POP) is chemically calcium sulphate hemihydrate, written as 2CaSO4.H2O (i.e., (CaSO4)2.H2O), meaning two units of calcium sulphate share one water molecule. (प्लास्टर ऑफ पेरिस — कैल्शियम सल्फेट हेमीहाइड्रेट)

 

• It is obtained by heating gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O) to about 373 K (120-150°C), which drives off three-quarters of its water of crystallisation.

 

• When mixed with water, Plaster of Paris sets into a hard mass, regaining the water it lost, which is why it is used to make casts for setting fractured bones, moulds, and decorative items.

 

• The name comes from its historical production from the abundant gypsum deposits near Paris, France.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gypsum, the raw material for Plaster of Paris, has the formula CaSO4.2H2O and is also used in the manufacture of cement to regulate setting time.

 

• If gypsum is heated to a much higher temperature, it loses all its water and forms 'dead burnt plaster' (anhydrous CaSO4), which does not set with water.

 

NOTE

 

• 2CaSO4.2H2O (Option 1): Not the correct hydrate ratio for Plaster of Paris.

 

• 2MgSO4.H2O (Option 2): Magnesium sulphate compounds are not Plaster of Paris; the correct compound is calcium-based, not magnesium-based.

 

• 2MgSO4.7H2O (Option 3): This is not Plaster of Paris; a magnesium sulphate heptahydrate (Epsom salt is MgSO4.7H2O) is a different compound entirely.

question: ______ is the centre for the Indian Institution of Soil Science.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhopal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Institute of Soil Science (IISS) is headquartered at Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. (भारतीय मृदा विज्ञान संस्थान — भोपाल)

 

• IISS was established in 1988 and functions under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR).

 

• The institute conducts research on soil health, fertility management, and sustainable soil resource use for Indian agriculture.

 

• It plays a key role in initiatives like the Soil Health Card Scheme, providing scientific inputs on soil testing and nutrient management.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• ICAR runs numerous specialised institutes across India, such as the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi and the Central Rice Research Institute, Cuttack.

 

• Bhopal also hosts other important national institutions, reflecting Madhya Pradesh's role as a hub for agricultural and scientific research.

 

NOTE

 

• Porbandar (Option 1): Known as the birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi, not the centre of IISS.

 

• Vishakhapatnam (Option 3): An important port city in Andhra Pradesh, not the location of IISS.

 

• Bhubaneswar (Option 4): Capital of Odisha, home to institutes like the Central Rice Research Institute region facilities, but not IISS.

question: In 1873, the Satyashodhak Samaj was established in ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay Presidency.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotirao (Jyotiba) Phule in 1873 at Pune, which was then part of the Bombay Presidency. (सत्यशोधक समाज — बॉम्बे प्रेसीडेंसी)

 

• The organisation aimed to fight against caste discrimination and Brahmanical dominance, and to secure equal rights for the lower castes and women.

 

• Jyotirao Phule is also known for his pioneering work in girls' education, having started one of India's first schools for girls in Pune in 1848 along with his wife Savitribai Phule.

 

• Phule was given the title 'Mahatma' in recognition of his social reform work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Phule's major work 'Gulamgiri' (Slavery), published in 1873, criticised the caste system and Brahmanical hegemony.

 

• The Satyashodhak Samaj movement later influenced leaders such as Shahu Maharaj of Kolhapur and contributed to the wider non-Brahmin movement in Maharashtra.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar Province (Option 1): Not the location; Satyashodhak Samaj was founded in western India.

 

• Madras Presidency (Option 2): Not the location; this region saw its own reform movements like the Self-Respect Movement, distinct from Satyashodhak Samaj.

 

• Punjab Province (Option 4): Not the location; Punjab was instead home to reform bodies like the Singh Sabha and Arya Samaj.

question: _______ are those where a monthly instalment is deposited in the accounts every month.
solution_text:
The correct answer is recurring deposits.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Recurring Deposit (RD) is a type of bank deposit in which the account holder deposits a fixed instalment every month for a chosen tenure, earning interest similar to a fixed deposit. (आवर्ती जमा — रिकरिंग डिपॉजिट)

 

• On maturity, the depositor receives the total of all instalments plus the interest accumulated, making it a popular tool for disciplined, small-scale saving.

 

• RD accounts are offered by both commercial banks and post offices, and typically have tenures ranging from 6 months to 10 years.

 

• Unlike a savings account, money in an RD cannot usually be withdrawn before maturity without a penalty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A Fixed Deposit (FD) involves depositing a lump sum amount once for a fixed period, unlike the monthly instalments of an RD.

 

• A Savings Bank Account allows deposits and withdrawals at any time and offers comparatively lower interest than RDs or FDs.

 

NOTE

 

• Savings bank deposits (Option 1): These allow flexible deposits/withdrawals anytime, not fixed monthly instalments.

 

• Reinvestment deposits (Option 2): These are deposits where interest earned is reinvested/compounded rather than paid out, not monthly instalment deposits.

 

• Fixed deposits (Option 3): These involve a single lump-sum deposit for a fixed tenure, not recurring monthly instalments.

question: When a magnesium ribbon is burnt in oxygen, it gets converted to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is magnesium oxide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a magnesium ribbon burns in oxygen (or air), it produces a dazzling white light and forms a white powder called magnesium oxide (MgO). (मैग्नीशियम ऑक्साइड — दहन अभिक्रिया)

 

• The balanced chemical reaction is: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO. This is a classic example of a combination (synthesis) reaction as well as an oxidation reaction.

 

• Because of the intense white light produced, burning magnesium ribbon was historically used in early photography flashbulbs and is still used in flares and fireworks.

 

• Magnesium oxide is a basic oxide; when dissolved in water it forms magnesium hydroxide (Mg(OH)2), a mild base.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Magnesium hydroxide is the active ingredient in antacids like milk of magnesia.

 

• Combustion of metals in oxygen generally forms their respective metal oxides, e.g., sodium burns to form sodium oxide, and iron rusts (slow oxidation) to form iron oxide.

 

NOTE

 

• Magnesium peroxide (Option 1): Not the product of simple combustion of magnesium in oxygen; it is a different, less common compound (MgO2).

 

• Magnesium hydroxide (Option 2): This is formed when magnesium oxide reacts with water, not directly from burning magnesium in oxygen.

 

• Magnesium carbonate (Option 3): This compound forms from magnesium reacting with carbon dioxide/carbonate sources, not from burning in oxygen.

question: Which of the following rocks may contain fossils of plants, animals and other microorganisms that once lived on them?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sedimentary rocks.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sedimentary rocks are formed by the deposition and compaction of sediments (weathered rock particles, organic matter) over long periods, which allows remains of plants, animals and microorganisms to get trapped and preserved as fossils. (तलछटी चट्टान — जीवाश्म)

 

• Because sedimentary rocks form in layers (strata) at relatively low temperature and pressure, organic remains are not destroyed during rock formation, unlike in igneous or metamorphic rocks.

 

• Common sedimentary rocks include sandstone, limestone, and shale, many of which are important sources of fossil fuels as well as fossil records.

 

• The study of fossils found in sedimentary rocks (paleontology) helps scientists reconstruct the history of life on Earth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Igneous rocks (e.g., granite, basalt) form from the cooling and solidification of molten magma/lava, temperatures at which any organic material would be destroyed.

 

• Metamorphic rocks (e.g., marble, slate) form when existing rocks are subjected to heat and pressure, which typically destroys any fossils that may have been present in the parent rock.

 

NOTE

 

• Metamorphic rocks (Option 1): Intense heat and pressure during metamorphism generally destroy fossil evidence.

 

• Intrusive igneous rocks (Option 2): Formed from magma cooling slowly below the earth's surface; the extreme heat prevents fossil preservation.

 

• Extrusive igneous rocks (Option 4): Formed from lava cooling rapidly at the surface; again, the high temperatures prevent fossils from forming.

question: Bade Ghulam Ali Khan was a prominent singer of the ______________ gharana.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Patiala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan was one of the most celebrated Hindustani classical vocalists and a leading exponent of the Patiala gharana. (पटियाला घराना — बड़े गुलाम अली खान)

 

• He was renowned for his mastery of the khayal form and popularised the light-classical thumri style, blending various gharana influences into his own distinctive style.

 

• He was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship and is remembered as one of the greatest vocalists of 20th-century Hindustani music.

 

• The Patiala gharana itself was founded by Ustad Fateh Ali Khan and Ustad Ali Baksh Khan in the princely state of Patiala, Punjab.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rampur-Sahaswan gharana is associated with vocalists like Ustad Mushtaq Hussain Khan.

 

• The Benaras gharana is well known for tabla and vocal music, while the Bhendi Bazaar gharana is associated with singers such as Anjanibai Malpekar.

 

NOTE

 

• Rampur Sahaswan (Option 1): A distinct gharana, not associated with Bade Ghulam Ali Khan.

 

• Benaras (Option 3): Known chiefly for its own tabla and vocal tradition, unrelated to Bade Ghulam Ali Khan.

 

• Bhendi Bazaar (Option 4): A separate Mumbai-based gharana, not Bade Ghulam Ali Khan's tradition.

question: Union Government has launched the Eighth Edition of Swachh Survekshan SS-2023 under Swachh Bharat Mission Urban 2.0. It is curated towards achieving circularity in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is waste management.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Swachh Survekshan 2023, the eighth edition of India's urban cleanliness survey, was launched under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban (SBM-U) 2.0 with the theme 'Waste to Wealth', aimed at achieving circularity in waste management. (स्वच्छ सर्वेक्षण 2023 — अपशिष्ट प्रबंधन में चक्रीयता)

 

• It was launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) and focuses on promoting the 3R principle — Reduce, Reuse, Recycle in urban solid waste management.

 

• Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0, launched in October 2021, aims to make all cities 'Garbage Free' and ensure grey and black water management in towns not covered under earlier phases.

 

• Swachh Survekshan has been conducted annually since 2016 and ranks Indian cities on cleanliness parameters, encouraging healthy competition among urban local bodies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Indore has consistently been ranked India's cleanest city in successive editions of the Swachh Survekshan.

 

• Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 October 2014, on the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Industrial management (Option 1): Not the focus area of Swachh Survekshan 2023, which targets urban solid waste.

 

• Roads management (Option 3): Not the specific circularity theme of this survey.

 

• Rainwater management (Option 4): Related to SBM-U 2.0's broader water management goals, but not the specific circularity focus of Swachh Survekshan 2023.

question: Which of the following is NOT a way in which a batsman can get out in a game of cricket?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Leg bye.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A 'leg bye' is a type of extra run scored when the ball, after hitting the batsman's body (not the bat), still results in a run being completed; it is not a mode of dismissal. (लेग बाई — आउट होने का तरीका नहीं)

 

• The recognised ways to dismiss a batsman in cricket include Bowled, Caught, Stumped, Leg Before Wicket (LBW), Run Out, Hit Wicket, Handled the Ball (obsolete now merged with obstructing the field), Hit the Ball Twice, Obstructing the Field, and Timed Out.

 

• Bowled occurs when the ball delivered by the bowler hits and disturbs the stumps.

 

• Stumped occurs when the wicketkeeper removes the bails while the batsman is out of the crease and not attempting a run, and LBW occurs when the ball would have hit the stumps but is intercepted by the batsman's body/leg while missing the bat.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Extras in cricket include byes, leg byes, wides, no-balls, and penalty runs — none of these, by themselves, is a mode of dismissal.

 

• The ICC Laws of Cricket (Law 30–39) formally define each of the ten ways a batsman can be given out.

 

NOTE

 

• Bowled (Option 1): This is a valid, recognised way of getting a batsman out.

 

• Stumped (Option 3): This is a valid, recognised way of getting a batsman out.

 

• Leg before wicket (Option 4): This is a valid, recognised way of getting a batsman out.

question: Ziyauddin Barani wrote his chronicle first in 1356 and another version _____ years later.
solution_text:
The correct answer is two.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ziyauddin Barani, a court historian under the Delhi Sultanate, wrote his famous chronicle 'Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi' first in 1356 CE, and produced a revised version around 1358 CE, i.e., two years later. (तारीख-ए-फ़िरोज़शाही — ज़ियाउद्दीन बरनी)

 

• The work covers the history of the Delhi Sultanate from the reign of Ghiyasuddin Balban (1266) to the early years of Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

 

• Barani revised his chronicle to bring the narrative up to date with the events of Firoz Shah Tughlaq's reign and to reflect his own political views and moral commentary.

 

• Barani is also known for his other major work, 'Fatawa-i-Jahandari', which discusses the theory of kingship and governance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Barani lived during the reigns of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firoz Shah Tughlaq, and his chronicles are a major primary source for the history of the Delhi Sultanate.

 

• Other important contemporary/near-contemporary Delhi Sultanate chroniclers include Amir Khusrau and Shams-i-Siraj Afif.

 

NOTE

 

• three (Option 1): Not the correct gap between the two versions of Barani's chronicle.

 

• eight (Option 2): Not the correct gap; this overstates the interval considerably.

 

• five (Option 4): Not the correct gap between the two versions of the chronicle.

question: If the State government dissolves the Panchayati Raj Institutions before the end of their five-year term, fresh elections should ordinarily be held within _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is six months.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Article 243E of the Indian Constitution, if a Panchayat is dissolved before the completion of its five-year term, elections to constitute a new Panchayat must ordinarily be completed within six months of the date of its dissolution. (पंचायत विघटन — छह माह में चुनाव)

 

• This provision was introduced by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).

 

• Article 243E also mandates that the newly constituted Panchayat shall continue only for the remainder of the original five-year period, not a fresh full term.

 

• However, this six-month timeline does not apply if the remainder of the period is less than six months, in which case fresh elections need not be held.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 added Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) to the Constitution, establishing a three-tier Panchayati Raj system.

 

• A parallel provision, Article 243U, prescribes the same six-month rule for Municipalities under the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.

 

NOTE

 

• One month (Option 1): Too short; not the constitutionally mandated timeframe.

 

• One year (Option 3): Too long; exceeds the six-month limit set under Article 243E.

 

• Three months (Option 4): Not the correct timeframe under Article 243E.

question: Which of the following categories did Ram Sahay Panday receive the Padma Shri 2022 in?
option_2: Distinguished service in the field of art
solution_text:
The correct answer is Distinguished service in the field of art.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ram Sahay Panday, a veteran Rai folk dance artist from Madhya Pradesh (Bundelkhand region), was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 in the 'Art' category, for his distinguished service in preserving and popularising the Rai folk dance form. (राई लोक नृत्य — रामसहाय पांडे)

 

• He dedicated decades of his life to promoting Rai dance, a traditional folk dance form of the Bundelkhand and Baghelkhand regions, and trained numerous artists to keep the tradition alive.

 

• The Padma Awards are India's highest civilian honours (after the Bharat Ratna), given in categories such as Art, Literature & Education, Social Work, Public Affairs, Science & Engineering, Trade & Industry, Medicine, Civil Service, and Sports.

 

• Ram Sahay Panday passed away in 2024 at the age of 92, having received wide recognition for his lifelong contribution to folk art.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Teejan Bai, a renowned Pandavani singer from Chhattisgarh, is another notable Padma awardee associated with folk performing arts of central India.

 

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, following the Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan.

 

NOTE

 

• Carnatic Music (Option 1): Not Ram Sahay Panday's field; Carnatic music is a South Indian classical music tradition unrelated to Rai folk dance.

 

• Instrumentalist (Option 3): Not his category; he is recognised as a folk dance artist, not an instrumentalist.

 

• Singing (Option 4): Not his category; his contribution lies in folk dance, not vocal singing.

question: Which of the following Articles states that a State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 15.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 15 of the Indian Constitution states that the State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them. (अनुच्छेद 15 — भेदभाव का निषेध)

 

• Article 15 falls under Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution, specifically under the Right to Equality.

 

• It also empowers the State to make special provisions for women, children, and socially/educationally backward classes, including SCs and STs (via subsequent amendments such as the 93rd Amendment enabling reservations in education).

 

• Article 15 works alongside Article 14 (equality before law) and Article 16 (equality of opportunity in public employment) to form the constitutional bedrock of non-discrimination.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 17 abolishes 'untouchability' in any form, while Article 18 abolishes titles (except military and academic distinctions).

 

• The Right to Equality (Articles 14-18) is one of the six Fundamental Rights guaranteed under the Indian Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 59 (Option 2): Deals with conditions of the President's office, unrelated to non-discrimination.

 

• Article 25 (Option 3): Guarantees freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion, not the non-discrimination clause.

 

• Article 40 (Option 4): A Directive Principle directing the State to organise village panchayats, unrelated to this provision.

question: The Paramhans Mandali was established to work for the abolition of caste in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1840.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Paramhans Mandali was established in 1840 in Bombay (Maharashtra) to work towards the abolition of caste distinctions and to promote rational, monotheistic religious belief among its members. (परमहंस मंडली — जाति उन्मूलन)

 

• It was founded largely through the efforts of reformers associated with the Manav Dharma Sabha, and its early members included figures like Dadoba Pandurang.

 

• Members of the Paramhans Mandali secretly rejected caste and idol worship, and would sometimes symbolically break caste taboos, such as eating food prepared by people of different castes.

 

• The Mandali operated in a fairly secretive manner given the strong social backlash faced by anti-caste reformers at the time, and it eventually declined by the 1860s.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Paramhans Mandali is considered a precursor to later reform movements such as the Prarthana Samaj, founded in 1867 in Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang.

 

• Other major 19th-century socio-religious reform organisations include the Brahmo Samaj (1828, Raja Ram Mohan Roy) and the Arya Samaj (1875, Swami Dayanand Saraswati).

 

NOTE

 

• 1830 (Option 1): Not the correct year of the Mandali's founding.

 

• 1820 (Option 3): Not the correct year of the Mandali's founding.

 

• 1850 (Option 4): Not the correct year of the Mandali's founding.

question: What is the suffix for –OH group according to IUPAC?
solution_text:
The correct answer is -ols.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to IUPAC nomenclature, the hydroxyl (-OH) functional group is denoted using the suffix '-ol', as in compounds like methanol, ethanol, and propanol. (हाइड्रॉक्सिल समूह — प्रत्यय 'ओल')

 

• The -OH group characterises the class of organic compounds called alcohols, and the suffix is added after dropping the terminal 'e' of the corresponding alkane name (e.g., ethane → ethanol).

 

• IUPAC nomenclature uses standard suffixes to denote different functional groups uniformly, ensuring that a compound's structure can be identified from its name.

 

• For example, ethanol (C2H5OH) is systematically named using the parent chain 'ethane' with the '-ol' suffix replacing the final 'e'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The suffix '-ene' denotes a carbon-carbon double bond (alkenes, e.g., ethene), and '-one' denotes a ketone functional group (e.g., propanone/acetone).

 

• The suffix '-ane' (or plural '-anes') denotes saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) with only single bonds, e.g., methane, ethane.

 

NOTE

 

• -ene (Option 2): This suffix denotes a double bond (alkenes), not the -OH group.

 

• -one (Option 3): This suffix denotes a ketone (carbonyl group), not the -OH group.

 

• -anes (Option 4): This suffix denotes saturated alkanes, not the -OH group.

question: What is the duration of the lunch interval in a cricket test match?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 40 minutes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a Test cricket match, the standard lunch interval is 40 minutes, as per the ICC's Standard Test Match Playing Conditions. (लंच इंटरवल — 40 मिनट)

 

• A Test match day is generally divided into three sessions, separated by the lunch break (40 minutes) and the tea break (20 minutes).

 

• These interval durations can occasionally be adjusted by on-field officials due to circumstances like bad light or rain delays, but 40 minutes for lunch is the standard duration.

 

• A full day's play in a Test match typically consists of a minimum of 90 overs, scheduled across the three sessions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tea interval in a Test match is usually 20 minutes, shorter than the lunch break.

 

• In ODIs, the break between innings is typically 10 minutes (extended in some formats), and in T20Is it's usually around 10-20 minutes, both shorter than a Test match's lunch break.

 

NOTE

 

• 25 minutes (Option 1): Not the standard duration of the Test match lunch interval.

 

• 35 minutes (Option 2): Not the standard duration of the Test match lunch interval.

 

• 30 minutes (Option 3): Not the standard duration of the Test match lunch interval.

question: In 1653, which French scientist observed that if some pressure is applied to any point of an incompressible fluid, the same pressure is transmitted to all points of the fluid and to the walls of the vessel?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Blaise Pascal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The French scientist Blaise Pascal, in 1653, formulated what is now known as Pascal's Law, which states that pressure applied to an enclosed, incompressible fluid is transmitted equally in all directions to every point of the fluid and to the walls of the container. (पास्कल का नियम — ब्लेज़ पास्कल)

 

• This principle forms the theoretical basis for numerous hydraulic devices, such as hydraulic lifts, hydraulic brakes, and hydraulic presses.

 

• Pascal was a French mathematician, physicist, inventor, and philosopher, also known for his work on probability theory, the Pascal's triangle, and inventing an early mechanical calculator.

 

• The SI unit of pressure, the 'Pascal (Pa)', is named in his honour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Daniel Bernoulli is known for Bernoulli's principle, relating the speed of a fluid to its pressure, important in aerodynamics.

 

• Evangelista Torricelli invented the mercury barometer and is credited with discovering atmospheric pressure; the pressure unit 'torr' is named after him.

 

NOTE

 

• Daniel Bernoulli (Option 1): Known for Bernoulli's principle (fluid dynamics), not Pascal's Law on pressure transmission.

 

• Evangelista Torricelli (Option 2): Known for inventing the barometer, not this law of pressure transmission.

 

• Eugene Bourdon (Option 4): Known for inventing the Bourdon tube pressure gauge, not this fundamental law.

question: Identify a marine alga that is used as food.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sargassum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sargassum is a genus of brown marine algae that is widely used as food in various coastal cuisines, and is also a source of algin (alginic acid), used commercially in the food and pharmaceutical industries. (सारगासुम — समुद्री शैवाल, खाद्य उपयोग)

 

• Being a marine (saltwater) alga, Sargassum grows in oceans and is notably found forming large floating mats in regions like the Sargasso Sea in the Atlantic Ocean.

 

• Marine algae like Sargassum are rich in minerals, iodine, and dietary fibre, and are consumed in several Asian coastal cultures, particularly as soups and salads.

 

• In contrast, Ulothrix, Spirogyra, and Volvox are all freshwater algae, commonly found in ponds, ditches, and slow-moving freshwater bodies, not marine environments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Spirogyra is famous for its spiral-shaped chloroplasts and is often called 'pond silk' or 'water silk'.

 

• Volvox is a colonial green alga forming spherical colonies, and is often studied as an example of the evolution of multicellularity.

 

NOTE

 

• Ulothrix (Option 1): A filamentous freshwater green alga, not a marine food source.

 

• Spirogyra (Option 3): A freshwater green alga known for its spiral chloroplasts, not used as marine food.

 

• Volvox (Option 4): A freshwater colonial green alga, not a marine food source.

question: Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister has launched a 'Naari Ko Naman' scheme that will allow women passengers in the state to pay only ______ of the fare for their travel within the state.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 50%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister launched the 'Naari Ko Naman' scheme, under which women passengers travelling within the state on HRTC (Himachal Road Transport Corporation) buses pay only 50% of the ticket fare. (नारी को नमन योजना — 50% किराया रियायत)

 

• The scheme was launched as part of the state government's welfare measures aimed at empowering women and easing their financial burden on public transport.

 

• It applies to ordinary bus services of the HRTC for women travelling anywhere within Himachal Pradesh.

 

• The scheme reflects a broader trend among several Indian states of offering fare concessions to women on public transport to promote women's mobility and safety.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• HRTC (Himachal Road Transport Corporation) is the state-run public bus transport undertaking of Himachal Pradesh.

 

• Similar women's transport fare concession schemes have also been implemented in other states, such as Delhi's free bus travel scheme for women.

 

NOTE

 

• 40% (Option 1): Not the concession percentage offered under this scheme.

 

• 20% (Option 2): Not the concession percentage offered under this scheme.

 

• 30% (Option 3): Not the concession percentage offered under this scheme.

question: What was the duration of Rolling Plan in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1978 to 1980.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rolling Plan in India was in effect from 1978 to 1980, introduced by the Janata Party government after rejecting the Draft Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-79) of the previous government. (रोलिंग प्लान — 1978 से 1980)

 

• The concept of a Rolling Plan was proposed by economist Gunnar Myrdal, involving three types of plans prepared simultaneously: an annual budget plan, a plan for a fixed number of years to be revised yearly, and a long-term perspective plan.

 

• When the Congress government returned to power in 1980, it discontinued the Rolling Plan and replaced it with the Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-85).

 

• The Rolling Plan aimed to provide greater flexibility by revising targets every year based on the latest economic conditions, unlike the fixed five-year plans.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's Planning Commission was established in 1950, and the First Five-Year Plan ran from 1951 to 1956.

 

• The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015, which does not prepare formal Five-Year Plans.

 

NOTE

 

• 1975 to 1977 (Option 1): Not the correct duration of the Rolling Plan.

 

• 1977 to 1979 (Option 2): Not the correct duration of the Rolling Plan.

 

• 1976 to 1978 (Option 3): Not the correct duration of the Rolling Plan.

question: Who among the following was the founder of the Kanva dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vasudeva.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kanva dynasty was founded by Vasudeva (Kanva), a minister who overthrew the last Shunga ruler, Devabhuti, and established his own rule around 75 BCE. (कण्व वंश — वासुदेव कण्व)

 

• The Kanva dynasty ruled parts of Magadha (present-day Bihar) for a relatively short period after succeeding the Shunga dynasty.

 

• The dynasty had four rulers: Vasudeva, Bhumimitra, Narayana, and Susharman, the last of whom was overthrown by the Satavahanas around 30 BCE.

 

• Much of what is known about the Kanva dynasty comes from the Puranas, as very few independent inscriptions or coins from this period have survived.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Shunga dynasty, which preceded the Kanvas, was founded by Pushyamitra Shunga after he assassinated the last Mauryan ruler, Brihadratha, around 185 BCE.

 

• The Kanva dynasty was eventually succeeded by the Satavahana dynasty in the Deccan/Magadha region.

 

NOTE

 

• Narayana (Option 1): The third ruler of the Kanva dynasty, not its founder.

 

• Susharman (Option 2): The fourth and last ruler of the Kanva dynasty, not its founder.

 

• Devabhuti (Option 4): The last ruler of the preceding Shunga dynasty, who was overthrown by Vasudeva Kanva; not a Kanva ruler.

question: Who has been named as the new chief minister of Tripura in May 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manik Saha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Manik Saha was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Tripura in May 2022, succeeding Biplab Kumar Deb, who resigned ahead of the 2023 state assembly elections. (माणिक साहा — त्रिपुरा मुख्यमंत्री)

 

• He belongs to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and had previously served as the President of the BJP's Tripura state unit.

 

• Manik Saha is a dental surgeon by profession before entering full-time politics, and had also served as a Rajya Sabha MP prior to becoming Chief Minister.

 

• He continued as Chief Minister after leading the BJP to victory in the 2023 Tripura Legislative Assembly elections.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Biplab Kumar Deb, who preceded Manik Saha, had been Tripura's Chief Minister since 2018, when the BJP first came to power in the state.

 

• Tripura's capital is Agartala, and the state shares an international border with Bangladesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajiv Rajan (Option 1): Not a real/relevant chief ministerial figure of Tripura.

 

• Sangeeta Singh (Option 2): Not the Chief Minister of Tripura in May 2022.

 

• Mahesh Verma (Option 3): Not the Chief Minister of Tripura in May 2022.
